WoW: Forever

Feral — Cat Druid

Energy and combo points in Cat Form, on bleeds rather than big hits. From level 20 onward, one guide calls it "one of the fastest and most mobile specializations in the WoW Forever beta." Before 20 you are a bear.

WoW: Forever · Melee DPS · Updated October 5, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70124 · Null Ossuary

Levelling guide, 1 to 60. The beta is capped at level 30 as of the October 1 build, which Blizzard raised from 20 that day, so no level-60 Cat build has been tested. Bear and Cat share one talent tree and mostly one build; they have separate pages because the rotations, stat priorities and gear are completely different. No source has posted a level 30 build either — the cap only reached 30 on October 1 and none of the three has published one since — so the level 30 line below extends the published level 20 build using the full talent tree's point costs, not a build any guide has recommended. Blizzard's own caveat: "class abilities and talents may continue to evolve throughout the beta test and are subject to additional changes."

What Cat is for

Damage out of stealth, at speed, and on bleeds that keep ticking while you reposition: Feral Swiftness gives "a permanent 30% speed buff while in Cat Form" plus +4% dodge in all forms, and it now works indoors; you also have Prowl, shapeshifting breaks roots, and Rip scales with attack power and runs 12 seconds off five combo points.

The published assessment, which measures solo kill speed — and it only applies from 20, when Cat Form arrives: one guide calls Feral "one of the fastest and most mobile specializations in the WoW Forever beta."

Cat Form now comes from a quest chain, not a trainer. "In WoW Forever, druids earn Cat Form with a quest chain at level 20. Your trainer sends you to Moonglade, the Great Cat Spirit asks for three relics hidden in the Stormrage Barrow Dens, and when you bring them back your trainer teaches you Cat Form, Prowl, Claw and Rip in one go." It is 2,885 experience in total, and the relics are party loot: "Five druids in a group loot the relic once instead of five times."

Your talent points

Level 20: 0/11/0. Most sources publish one build shared with Bear; see the Bear page for its click order. The shared reasoning for Ferocity names both roles: it helps "your Rage economy while leveling" and reduces "your energy cost in Cat Form."

Two sources do split them at 20. The cat-specific lists are:

  • Dungeons: Ferocity 5 / Heart of the Wild 5 / Savage Fury 1
  • Duels: Ferocity 5 / Heart of the Wild 1 / Feral Swiftness 2 / Brutal Impact 2 / Savage Fury 1

Level 30: 0/21/0 — our own extension, not a published build. No source has posted one. Where Cat and Bear diverge on the shared tree:

TalentCatBear
Ferocity3/55/5
Heart of the Wild5/54/5
Feral Swiftness2/2—
Feral Instinct—3/3
Shredding Attacks3/3—
Primal Bite—1/1
Savage Fury, Feral Charge, Sharpened Claws, Blood Frenzy, Leader of the Packsamesame

Cat buys Feral Swiftness and Shredding Attacks (Shred's energy cost) and underfills Ferocity. Bear buys full Ferocity, Feral Instinct for Swipe, and Primal Bite. Both spend the twenty-first point on Leader of the Pack. A third reading stays deliberately dual-role at 30.

Rotation

At level 20 it is two buttons:

  1. Claw to build combo points
  2. Rip at 5 combo points

From 24 you add Rake. The published rotation also calls for Tiger's Fury here "when below 40 Energy" — drop that step. Tiger's Fury was removed outright in the October 1 build, not merely announced; it no longer exists to use. Shifting Power (below) is its replacement, but it is a row 4 talent behind Shredding Attacks, which Blizzard moved up to row 3 — both are out of reach this early.

From 30:

  1. Maintain Faerie Fire, usable in form now, and as of October 1 it no longer resets your swing timer when used
  2. Shred on Omen of Clarity procs. Omen is baseline at 20 in Forever, not a talent
  3. Maintain Rip at 5 combo points
  4. Maintain Rake
  5. Shred as filler, from behind

One correction to a widely-copied level-30 rotation: it calls for Ferocious Bite, which trains at level 32. You will not have it at a level-30 cap.

The target-selection rule: "pick Rip when the enemy will live through the ticks, and direct damage when the remaining kill time is too short. Keep an existing bleed running instead of restarting it."

Multi-target: there is none in Cat Form. Swipe is Bear-only. Either shift to Bear and Swipe, or spread Rake and Rip on targets durable enough to be worth it.

Stat priority

Agility first, then Strength, then Stamina.

The reason Agility leads is that "in cat form it is attack power, critical strike and armor at once."

The Forever-specific part reverses a Classic habit: your weapon's damage now counts in Cat Form. Cat Form's flat attack power was cut from 40 to 12 plus Agility, and abilities gained weapon-damage terms. Blizzard's own framing of the mechanism: auto-attack DPS in Cat Form now simply equals your weapon's DPS, at a fixed 1.0-second swing speed (2.5 seconds in Bear or Dire Bear Form), and weapon-damage abilities use the same numbers. The result: "the weapon here is chosen on its damage first, then on its stats." Published level-20 cat weapon picks are two-handers on both factions, held in both hands.

One source disputes the weapon-DPS priority outright. Three sources and the client data are against it, but the disagreement exists and no source publishes the actual conversion formula.

A level-20 cat has Claw, Rip and Prowl and nothing else. A level-30 cat still has no Ferocious Bite. Tiger's Fury, which older guides train at 24, no longer appears here: it was removed in the October 1 build, replaced by the Shifting Power talent (below).

What defines Cat

TalentEarliest levelWhat it does
Feral Swiftness 2/216+30% Cat movement speed and +4% dodge in all forms. Renamed from Feline Swiftness. Moved from row 3 to row 2; Blizzard confirms the speed bonus now works indoors and the dodge bonus applies all the time, not only in Cat Form
Shifting PowerRow 4, 16-point gold medalLive as of October 1. Connected to Shredding Attacks in row 4. Cat Form only, 16-second cooldown. Costs 55% of base Mana, instantly converted into 40 Energy. Cost is reduced by effects that reduce Shapeshifting cost, and it costs the same Mana as Cat Form itself
Improved Shifting PowerNew, Row 5Requires Shifting Power. Reduces its cooldown by 4/8 seconds per rank — 2/2 brings it from 16 seconds down to 8
Feral Charge11-point gold medalShared with Bear. Blizzard: it now also grants a Cat Form version, 30-second cooldown, that does not interrupt or immobilize the target — Cat's first dedicated gap-closer
Rend and Tear 5/539New. +10% melee damage against bleeding targets, which is why bleeds now matter more than Shred
Berserk40The 31-point capstone — 15-second duration, 3-minute cooldown — and it needs Leader of the Pack first. For a Cat it is +100% crit on combo-point generators for 15 seconds and fear immunity. The three-target Primal Bite clause needs Bear or Dire Bear, so it is not a Cat cleave

What Forever changed for Cat

  • The old Furor powershifting trick is dead, but Blizzard has deliberately reintroduced the gameplay in a different form — this is confirmed by Blizzard, not a player rumour. Furor was rewritten: instead of a flat 40 energy on entering Cat Form, five points let you regenerate Energy out of form "as if they were in Cat Form" — and Blizzard states the penalty in the same breath: "But if they go to Bear Form, all that Energy is lost, to prevent 'bear-weaving' gameplay." The numbers are client text, not published: the tooltip reads "regain 100% of the Energy you had when you were last in Cat Form, plus 10 Energy for each second you spent not in Bear Form, Cat Form, or Dire Bear Form, up to a maximum of 100" at 5/5, and "Leaving an empty bar and instantly re-entering supplies no flat refill." Blizzard then adds: "We realize this removed the 'power shifting' gameplay some players prize, so we have re-added that gameplay in a much more approachable way with the Shifting Power talent in the Feral talent tree." That talent is live as of October 1 — see Shifting Power above for its numbers.
  • Tiger's Fury was removed in the October 1 build — this is now live, not merely announced. Blizzard's class deep dive first flagged it under baseline shapeshifting changes: "Tiger's Fury: (Removed.) This has been replaced with a new Feral-specific talent called Shifting Power." The October 1 Development Notes confirm the ability itself is gone from the build — the datamined Tiger's Fury rework some guides still describe (no cost, 30-second cooldown, flat +15% physical damage) never shipped and will not appear; Shifting Power (above) is what replaced it, live with full numbers the same day.
  • Bleeds carry the spec now, and Shred got stronger too. Blizzard: Shred’s "damage increased significantly to need less talent support to be effective" — no figures are published either way. Rip was buffed enormously. Rank 6 deals 243/396/549/702/855 over 12 seconds by combo point, against Classic's 45/73/101/129/157, and it now scales with attack power.
  • Claw became a weapon-damage multiplier: "110% normal damage plus 27", where Classic gave a flat "27 additional damage." Ferocious Bite is unchanged from Classic, and trains at 32.
  • Cat Form's flat attack power was cut from 40 to 12 plus Agility. This is the mechanism behind the weapon change.
  • New talents, net of October 1: Primal Bite, Predatory Strikes, Natural Reaction, Rend and Tear, Berserk, Shifting Power, Improved Shifting Power. King of the Jungle was also new to Forever but has now been removed outright — it is gone from the tree, not merely absent from a build list, and the old caveat about its tooltip not matching Tiger's Fury's removal no longer applies because the talent itself is gone. Heart of the Wild moved to tier 1. Feral Instinct was rewritten from bear threat to +30% Swipe damage.
  • A rename and a merge, both confirmed directly by Blizzard's class deep dive: Mangle is now the Primal Bite talent and is gone from the spellbook — "We have opted to go with this ability instead of Mangle." Classic's Primal Fury and Blood Frenzy were merged into one node, and Blizzard's own text says the merged node is Blood Frenzy: "The effects of the old Primal Fury and Blood Frenzy talent have been combined into this single 2-point talent." It gained a cat clause giving combo-point generators a chance at an extra point on a crit. Primal Fury is not selectable, so lists naming it cannot be entered as printed.
  • Periodic effects were fixed to allow critical hits one at a time, not as a blanket rule. On the Druid side Blizzard names Rejuvenation, Tranquility and Wild Growth; elsewhere Renew, Devouring Plague, Riptide, Lacerating Strikes, Hellfire and Contingency Plan. October 1 ran the other way for one case — Gnome’s Eureka! "no longer benefits periodic effects at all."

At level 60

Unknown. The open question is whether bleed-centric damage with Rend and Tear beats a Rogue once Berserk and real weapons exist.

Sources

Compiled from the three major Forever guide sites and cross-checked against each other. Where Blizzard has published an official class deep dive, that post outranks all three and the page is written from it. Everything else — talent ranks, tooltip values, what exists in the tree at all — is settled against the client itself, read through foreverchanges.pro and wago.tools. Where the guides disagree with each other, this page says which said what.
